label: Late absolute position: <DEL> of length-9 sequences and copy steps at t>=14
explanation: Never active during the original-input phase (t<=5 essentially zero). Active only at the delimiter and in the copy phase, and the firing rate depends mostly on absolute step t: at the <DEL> step it fires 12% overall, mostly for long sequences (L=9 at t=9). In the copy phase the rate climbs steadily with t, from about 6% at t=12 to 24% at t=14, 37% at t=15, 54% at t=16 and 60% at t=17, so it concentrates on the last few outputs of long (L=8-9) sequences. It almost never fires at recall_idx 1-3. The predicate (t>=14) or (<DEL> with L=9) gets dev F1 0.53 and mass recall 0.82. Precision is only about 0.4: even in these late positions it fires on less than half the steps, and which ones depends weakly on content. Rate is higher when the input or output token is a digit (0, 1, 2) or f/h/n, and when the sequence has many digits (n_digits 0: 3%, n_digits 4: 13%), but no token rule I tried fixed precision. The largest activations are at <DEL> of L=9 sequences beginning with f or 0, and at late copy steps outputting 0 or f.
